articles.author: Logic Verse
articles.description:
Nvidia’s reported discussions involving AI hardware startup Groq have sparked fresh debate across the semiconductor and artificial intelligence ecosystem. The move is trending as AI workloads increasingly shift from training models to running them efficiently in production environments. Groq is known for its purpose-built inference hardware, while Nvidia dominates the AI accelerator market through GPUs. Any form of partnership, investment, or technical collaboration would signal a meaningful evolution in Nvidia’s long-term AI strategy. Cloud providers, enterprises, and AI developers are closely watching the development for clues about the next phase of AI infrastructure.
Background & Context
generative AI applications matured, inference workloads began to dominate real-world usage. Inference demands lower latency, predictable performance, and better cost efficiency at scale. Groq entered this space with its Language Processing Unit architecture, designed specifically for deterministic, high-throughput inference. Growing interest in Groq’s approach reflects wider industry pressure to diversify beyond GPU-centric architectures as AI adoption accelerates globally.
Key Facts / What Happened
Voices & Perspectives
A senior semiconductor executive noted, “Purpose-built chips like LPUs are forcing established players to rethink how heterogeneous AI systems are designed.”
Implications
What’s Next / Future Outlook
end-to-end AI platform. Groq could gain wider enterprise visibility if collaborations materialize. The next wave of AI infrastructure announcements will increasingly focus on inference benchmarks rather than training scale alone.
Our Take
Wrap-Up
As AI moves from experimentation to everyday deployment, inference efficiency is becoming the new battleground. Whether or not a formal deal emerges, Nvidia and Groq’s alignment reflects where the industry is heading next.
articles.title: Nvidia–Groq Talks Signal New Shift in the AI Chip Race

Khi làm việc với XDocReport để populate data từ field vào các placeholder trong DocX template, một trong những thứ cần quan tâm là phải tạo các placeholder bằng plugin được phát triển bởi XDocReport. Lý do đằng sau là do Word không đảm bảo việc một word/placeholder luôn luôn được lưu trữ, tokeninze trong internal data structure (zip format, xml format) với cùng định dạng khi rendered trên word. 
Ví dụ: placeholder:
{full_name}

có thể được lưu trữ thành:
<tag>{full</tag><tagb>_name}</tagb>

thay vì
{full_name}

vì vậy để replace placeholder bằng các hàm string replace là không hoàn toàn khả thi, và có khả năng gây lỗi bất cứ khi nào. 
Ref: https://gpcoder.com/3185-huong-dan-xuat-du-lieu-ra-file-word-pdf-voi-xdocreport/
articles.title: XDocReport cần plugin để tạo placeholder

Prompts used to be just text.
You wrote a few sentences, pasted them into a chat box, tweaked the wording, and moved on. If the output was not good, you tried again. Nothing else depended on it. The cost of getting it wrong was close to zero.
That phase did not last long. In The Turning Point of AI, I shared that:
AI isn’t just a tool for completing your sentences or suggesting the next line of code. We need to see it as a new way of building software.
The moment prompts moved out of chat windows and into those systems, their role changed. They were no longer throwaway text. They were reused across flows. They carried logic. They returned structured data that other parts of the system depended on.
At that point, prompts quietly became part of the system.

articles.author: Puneet-Kumar2010
articles.description:
Most game AIs are fake smart.

Patterns, scripts, predictable behavior.
Block-Reign isn’t.
This is a lightweight Player vs AI grid battle game where the AI actually learns from every match you play — wins, losses, mistakes, all of it.
No GPU.

No fancy engines.

Just Python, reinforcement learning, and persistence.
Block-Reign is a 10×10 grid-based Player vs AI combat game built with:
Flask + HTML for the frontend
Python for the game server
Reinforcement Learning (Q-Learning) for live gameplay
DQN for advanced offline experimentation
You play in the browser.

The AI plays on the server.

After every match, it gets smarter.
The core idea was simple:
What if the AI learned only from real games — not pre-trained data?
So the AI:
Starts dumb
Learns only from actual matches

Saves its knowledge permanently
Adapts to your playstyle



No synthetic data.

No scripted behaviors.

Just experience.
The running server uses a Q-learning AI

After each completed match:


Match data is sent to the server
The AI updates its Q-table
Progress is saved on disk
Restart the server → the AI remembers everything
The project also includes a DQN trainer (ai_trainer.py) for experimentation.
As of the latest run:
Win rate: ~59%
Matches played: 78
Record: 46 Wins / 36 Losses
These stats are not hardcoded.

They are learned, stored, and persisted.
Delete the training folder, and the AI forgets everything.
10×10 grid
Arrow keys to move
Space to shoot
Simple mechanics, strategic positioning
Fast matches, instant feedback
Minimal visuals.

Maximum behavior learning.
Delete:
training/

or:
training/models/simple_ai.pkl

Restart the server and play again.

The AI starts from scratch.
This project wasn’t about graphics or polish.
It was about:
Understanding reinforcement learning
Watching an AI evolve organically
Building adaptive systems without massive compute
https://github.com/DeveloperPuneet/Block-Reign
Block-Reign isn’t perfect.

But it’s honest.
An AI that earns its intelligence one loss at a time.
And nah — this isn’t the end.
comment
articles.title: Block-Reign: A Player vs AI Grid Game That Learns From You

Zero Install, Zero Setup: The Fastest Way to Track Your Life Metrics.



Your personal space to track habits, mood, and progress with customizable widgets.

In an era of mandatory logins, monthly subscriptions, and invasive data harvesting, there is something revolutionary about a tool that lives entirely within a single HTML file.
The Dashboard of Life is a minimalist, high-utility personal metrics tracker designed for users who value speed, privacy, and simplicity. It allows for the tracking of hydration, mood, reading progress, or any custom habit without a single byte of data leaving the local machine.
Most modern productivity apps require a cloud connection. This dashboard flips the script by utilizing the browser's native capabilities. By leveraging Local Storage, the application persists data across sessions without the need for a back-end database.
Zero Registration Required: There are no "Sign Up" buttons. The tool is ready to use the moment the file is opened.
No Installation or Downloads: It runs directly in any modern web browser. No .exe or .dmg installers are necessary.
Absolute Privacy: Data is stored locally in the browser. No external servers ever see the personal metrics, moods, or habits being tracked.
Total Data Ownership: The built-in Export/Import functionality allows users to save their data as a JSON file. This ensures that even if browser history is cleared, the data remains portable and secure.
Developers and privacy enthusiasts are increasingly moving toward "local-first" software. This dashboard eliminates "subscription fatigue" and the risk of data breaches. It is a clean, "set it and forget it" solution for anyone looking to optimize their life without sacrificing their digital footprint.
Experience the simplicity of the Ultimate 'Ghost' Dashboard: Manage your life without leaving a digital footprint.
articles.title: Is This the Most Private Way to Track Your Life? Dashboard of Life.
